title: Civil Petition / Account — Thomas Smith v. James M. Wrenn, Cedar County, Missouri, March Term 1867
text:
State of Missouri }
                  }  In the Circuit
County of Cedar  }
                     Court of Cedar County
                     Mo. March Term 1867
Thomas Smith Plaintiff }
           against      }
James M. Wrenn Def[endant] }

Plaintiff states that the defendant owes him One hundred Dollars for
the price and value of one yoke of work
cattle sold and delivered by the plaintiff
to the Defendant. Also the said
Defendant owes plaintiff Twenty one & 70
Dollars for money paid    and expenses
by plaintiff for the Defendant at his
request. The pore[?] years of all of which
Also the already thereof will appear by
an account & hereunto filed. Plaintiff
asks judgment for Twenty two & 70 dollars
being the balance due him.
Chandler & Buckley Atty[?].

Thomas Smith in a/c with James M. Wrenn
1866
Oct 28th  For one yoke of Work Cattle  $100
Oct 24th  Amount paid on note for [?] money  $7.25[?]
          and paid on note for Mrs. Rains  $1000[?]

Total  $114.85[?]
James M. Wrenn Cr.
Feb 20, 1866  Rec'd from John[?] Eagle on a/c[?]
              of land bargained to him  $25.00
              Balance due Thos. Smith  $7.285[?]
notes: Handwritten petition and account statement in the civil case Thomas Smith v. James M. Wrenn. Smith claims Wrenn owes $100 for a yoke of work cattle sold and delivered, plus $21.70 for money paid and expenses, totaling amounts with a balance claimed of $22.70 (or $7.285 per the account). Numbers in the account are somewhat difficult to read — dollar amounts transcribed as best estimates. Attorneys listed as Chandler & Buckley. Several words and dollar figures are uncertain due to cursive handwriting.
